candidates.explanation: I couldn't open the file, so this diagnosis comes from the snippets and the usual structure of this boilerplate. refreshToken does not appear to invalidate the old refresh token. The session's stored hash is probably not compared with `data.hash`, or it is not rotated and saved (`sessionService.update(session.id, { hash })`) before the new pair is issued. The new tokens may also be built with the old hash. In either case the old refresh token's session and hash stay valid, so it can be replayed any number of times.

The controller passes the sessionId and hash from the JWT payload to the service and does nothing else. All replay protection therefore depends on the service's hash check and rotation, which look missing.

The refresh token is signed with the hash passed in by the caller. If refreshToken passes the old session hash, or never rotates it, the new refresh token carries the same hash and the old one stays valid.

fix.description: In refreshToken, load the session by `data.sessionId` and throw UnauthorizedException if it is missing or if `session.hash !== data.hash`. Then generate a new random hash (for example, sha256 of a random string) and persist it with `sessionService.update(session.id, { hash })` before issuing tokens. Pass the new hash to getTokensData so the new refresh token carries it. Any later use of the old token then fails the hash comparison.
